marks.gloss_en: כדתניא: וטמא טמא יקרא -- he must make it known to the many, and the many ask mercy for him; and so one to whom something happened
the baraita: 'and he shall cry: impure, impure' (Lev 13:45) -- he must make it known to the many
כי היכי דליחזיוהו אינשי וליבעו רחמי עילויה -- so that people see it and ask mercy for it (= p_sikra_rachamim)
the stam: [the red paint is] so that people will see it and ask mercy for it
Ravina: like whom do we hang date-clusters on a palm? like this tanna
[the prohibition of] it and its offspring applies both in the Land and outside the Land
both non-sacred, both slaughtered outside: the first is fit
both sacrificial, both slaughtered outside: the first is liable to karet
both non-sacred, both slaughtered inside: the first is unfit
first non-sacred, second sacrificial, both outside: the first is fit
first sacrificial, second non-sacred, both outside: the first is liable to karet
first non-sacred, second sacrificial, both inside: the first is unfit
both non-sacred, first outside, second inside: the first is fit
both sacrificial, first outside, second inside: the first is liable to karet
both non-sacred, first inside, second outside: the first is unfit

'when a bull, sheep or goat is born... it may be accepted for an offering' (Lev 22:27) and after it 'you shall not slaughter it and its offspring in one day' (22:28): the juxtaposition teaches that it applies to sacrificial animals
the baraita: it and its offspring applies to sacrificial animals, from the juxtaposition of Lev 22:27 and 22:28
ואימא: במוקדשין -- אין, בחולין -- לא! -- given the juxtaposition, perhaps it applies only to sacrificial animals
״שור״ הפסיק העניין -- the repeated 'bull' breaks off the topic of offerings
ואימא: בחולין -- אין, במוקדשין -- לא! -- then perhaps only non-sacred animals
כתיב ״ושור״ -- וי״ו מוסיף על עניין ראשון: the vav adds to the first topic, so sacrificial animals are included too
אי מה קדשים כלאים לא, אף אותו ואת בנו כלאים לא? אלמה תניא: נוהג בכלאים -- if it is juxtaposed to offerings, it should exclude kilayim as offerings do
the baraita: it and its offspring applies to the offspring of diverse kinds
ועוד, ״שה״ כתיב, ואמר רבא: זה בנה אב -- כל מקום שנאמר שה אינו אלא להוציא את הכלאים
